facts.content: Patient reports right knee pain with clicking during runs.
facts.source_text: CC: R knee pain w/ clicking during runs

facts.content: Patient reports intermittent tingling in the right toes after runs.
facts.source_text: intermittent tingling in R toes post-run

facts.content: Right knee pain and clicking began approximately two weeks ago.
Patient has been marathon training for one month, running 4 to 8 miles.
facts.source_text: Context: Marathon training x1 mo; runs 4–8 mi

facts.content: Patient goes to the gym three times per week.
Patient plays ice hockey and had a fall with a large bruise months ago.
facts.source_text: plays ice hockey (fall w/ large bruise months ago)

facts.content: Right knee pain starts about 20 minutes into a run, around 3 miles.
facts.source_text: Pain: Starts ~20 min into run (~3 mi)

facts.content: Right knee pain worsens with gym abdominal work involving knee flexion and extension.
facts.source_text: worse w/ gym ab work (knee flex/extend)

facts.content: The patient is currently pain-free at rest.
Pain is located in the central right knee, sometimes slightly to the right side.
facts.source_text: Location: Central R knee, sometimes slightly to R side

facts.content: There was mild right knee swelling after the first run, which improved with ice, and there is no swelling currently.
facts.source_text: Swelling: Mild after first run, improved w/ ice; none currently

facts.content: Patient reports no giving way, no instability, and no locking of the knee.
facts.source_text: Function: No giving way/instability; no locking

facts.content: Stairs and walking are okay according to the patient.
The patient reports full knee flexion and extension.
There was a single episode of tingling in the right toes after a run, which resolved.
facts.source_text: Neurovasc: Single episode tingling R toes after run; resolved

facts.content: The patient reports no color or temperature change in the limb.
The patient reports no calf pain.
The patient notices sock indentation after prolonged standing.
facts.source_text: Other: Notices sock indentation after prolonged standing

facts.content: Patient is farsighted.
Patient has a history of a prior severe urinary tract infection requiring an emergency department visit.
Patient takes ibuprofen 400 mg as needed.
Patient takes Aleve.
Patient takes acetaminophen.
Patient takes vitamin D.
Patient takes melatonin as needed.
Patient rarely takes Xanax as needed.
Patient uses occasional cannabis.
Patient has right knee pain with mechanical symptoms in a runner of about two weeks' duration without instability or locking and transient right toe paresthesia after running.
facts.source_text: 1) R knee pain w/ mechanical sx in runner, ~2 wks, no instability/locking; transient R toe paresthesia post-run.

facts.content: Clinician assessment is that the symptoms are likely due to overuse.
Clinician notes that an in-person exam is needed to assess for intra-articular or ligamentous pathology if indicated.
facts.source_text: needs in-person exam to assess intra-articular/ligamentous pathology if indicated.

facts.content: Patient is advised to use ice therapy frequently.
Patient is advised to practice relative rest by easing up on running and not running through pain.
facts.source_text: • Relative rest: ease up on running; do not run through pain

facts.content: A stronger NSAID is prescribed electronically to be taken regularly with food, and the patient is instructed not to combine it with ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: • eRx stronger NSAID; take regularly w/ food; do not combine w/ ibuprofen

facts.content: Patient is referred to physiotherapy for assessment and examination and to determine the need for knee imaging based on findings.
facts.source_text: • Refer to physiotherapy for assessment/exam; determine need for knee imaging based on findings

facts.content: Patient is instructed to seek urgent care or call back if there is persistent swelling, heat or redness, fever or feeling unwell, or true locking of the knee.
facts.source_text: • Safety-net: seek urgent care/call back if persistent swelling, heat/redness, fever/feeling unwell, or true locking of knee

facts.content: Prescription was sent to the pharmacy.
